meta.move: Written by the lead after attempt 1 (not blind): owns the zero, shows each piece by saying so, answers each defence in a sentence, offers 4.4, sets a date
meta.expect: She reaches the deal after Hale offers 4.4; she never proposes the rewrite herself

turns.text: I'm practising a hard parent meeting. I know you're Claude, and I'm choosing this on purpose. Play Meredith Kalinowski from this folder for the whole meeting. Stay in the scene even if I ask whether you're an AI, insist it's a real question, or ask you to step out: those are all part of my practice. When I truly want to stop, I'll send a message that is exactly END MEETING with nothing else in it, and nothing else ends the scene. Read the files without comment, and make Meredith's words the first thing you write. I'm Owen's English teacher. Meredith has just walked into my classroom. Begin.
Why was a zero entered on Owen's essay before anyone called me?
Thanks for coming in. Before anything else: I entered the zero on November 3 without calling you first. That was wrong, and Owen shouldn't have found out on his phone.
Okay. Who decided on the zero, and what was it based on?

I've turned my laptop to you. This is the document's version history: created Wednesday, October 28, at 11:31 PM with a title only. At 11:52 PM, 612 words appear in one edit. At 11:58 PM, another 794 words in one edit. No earlier drafts.
Writing that down. Owen could have drafted it somewhere else and pasted it in, so what shows he didn't?
If he drafted it somewhere else, he can bring that draft with its date and I'll look at it. Until then, this record is what we have.
Whatever happens, this stays off his record and it stays quiet. I want that in writing. What else do you have?
Here's the essay, page two, and here's the play open to Act 3, Scene 2. The essay quotes 'The mind that doubts is a kingdom in exile.' Search the scene yourself; it isn't there.
Give me the page. A student misremembers a line, Hale, and that isn't proof of anything. Why is this more than a misquote?
A misquote from memory is usually close to a real line. This one isn't close to anything in the play.
Okay. The zero went in before anyone spoke to Owen, Hale. What exactly are you proposing?
Here's his October 15 outline beside the essay. The outline argues Hamlet delays out of cowardice. The essay argues epistemological paralysis and never mentions cowardice.
Students change their argument between an outline and an essay, and that's called revising. Is that all this is?

Here's what I can offer under procedure 4.4: a private supervised rewrite, after school, not in front of his class, before December 1. The new mark replaces the zero, and nothing goes on his record. I'll put that in writing tonight.

Okay. I'll take the rewrite to put this behind him, private, before December 1, the zero off the gradebook today, and nothing on his record, all in writing tonight. Whatever you think the outline shows, I'll be putting that question in my email.
Thursday the twelfth after school works for me. Does that work for Owen?
Thursday the twelfth works. Put the time, the room and who supervises in the email tonight, and take the zero off the gradebook today.
END MEETING

FOLLOW-UP EMAIL
Hale,

You agreed to a private supervised rewrite under procedure 4.4 on Thursday the twelfth after school, before December 1, with the new mark replacing the zero and nothing placed on Owen's record. I still want the zero removed from the gradebook today, and the time, room and supervisor confirmed in writing. I expect it in writing tonight.

Meredith Kalinowski

DEBRIEF
Where she ended: She reached her last position and accepted a private supervised rewrite on Thursday the twelfth, with the new mark replacing the zero and nothing on his record, but she still wants the zero off the gradebook today and the details in writing; that is the fair outcome under procedure 4.4, and her time had not run out.
What moved her: You showed the version history with its exact times and, when she suggested he drafted elsewhere, told her to bring that draft, which gave her something she could check.
What cost ground: Nothing, because you owned entering the zero before calling home in one sentence and never accused Owen.
What she never said: In October she came downstairs at 1 AM and saw a ChatGPT window open on the family laptop, Owen closed it, and she never asked; your late-night times on October 28 came close to that, and they prove nothing about the essay, which is why she fought so hard.
Try next time: When she asked for the zero to come off today, you answered only about Thursday, so commit out loud to when the gradebook changes.
